answer:
**The obstacle is softmax's denominator.** Attention needs normalized weights, and every weight depends on the sum of exponentials over all keys. A naive implementation stores all scores before normalizing. Online softmax instead maintains compact running statistics while processing blocks, allowing attention's weighted average to be accumulated without retaining every score. [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.14135)

**Why keep a running maximum?** Exponentiating a large raw score can overflow. Subtracting the maximum score makes all exponent arguments nonpositive, while leaving normalized probabilities unchanged. When a later block contains a larger maximum, earlier contributions must be rescaled to the new reference point.

**Work through scores 1 and 3.** After reading score 1 alone, the running maximum is 1 and the normalized-scale sum is $e^{1-1}=1$. On reading score 3, the maximum changes to 3. Rescale the previous sum to $e^{1-3}=e^{-2}$ and add the new contribution $e^{3-3}=1$. The final sum is $e^{-2}+1$, exactly what a stable softmax over both scores would use.

For values $v_1,v_2$, keep a running numerator too. It becomes $e^{-2}v_1+v_2$ under the new scale. Divide by $e^{-2}+1$ to obtain the same weighted output as ordinary attention. Apply this logic to entire blocks using their local maxima and sums.

**Be precise about what can stream.** Producing only the final weighted average needs running maximum, denominator, and value numerator. Producing every individual normalized probability also requires retaining or revisiting earlier scores, because the final denominator was not known when those scores arrived. This distinction explains how FlashAttention can avoid storing the attention matrix while still computing the exact attention output, up to floating-point ordering differences.

**Technical details and references.**

Maintain a running maximum m and sum l. When a block has maximum m_b, use m_new=max(m,m_b) and rescale the old sum by exp(m−m_new). Weighted-value numerators obey the same recurrence, enabling a true one-pass attention output without storing all pairwise scores. The file includes both blockwise attention and scalar softmax. Producing every normalized softmax probability requires a second pass or retention/rescaling of earlier outputs; claiming constant-memory single-pass output without either is misleading.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** With old maximum $m$ and new block maximum $m_b$, set $m'=\max(m,m_b)$ and $\ell'=e^{m-m'}\ell+\sum_{j\in block}e^{s_j-m'}$. Apply the same rescaling to the weighted-value numerator. Dividing the final numerator by $\ell$ recovers attention without retaining the full score matrix. [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.14135)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://huggingface.co/blog/garg-aayush/flash-attention) and [2](https://crfm.stanford.edu/2023/07/17/flash2.html).
